column2: Summary
column5: Description

column2: Verify the setup on every operating system the team uses
column5:
Plan ID: L-1 (wave 0)

Zone: Team
Depends on: nothing

In plain words (for beginners)
The setup instructions were written and tested on one Linux machine. Before real work starts we must know they also work on Windows and macOS. Every person follows docs/ONBOARDING.md on their own computer and reports what went wrong.

What
- Each teammate follows docs/ONBOARDING.md (or the PDF handbook) from step 1 to step 6 on their own computer.
- Write down every step that was unclear or failed (system, step number, the error text, a screenshot).
- Nour fixes the docs and scripts (setup.ps1, setup.sh, the winget/brew/apt commands) from the reports.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Windows, macOS and Linux each completed steps 1 to 6 at least once.
- ☐ Every reported problem is either fixed in the docs/scripts or has a ticket.
- ☐ The helper menu (tools/git-helper) starts on each system and option 2 ("Is my setup right?") is all green.

column2: Practice run (SCRUM-0) for every teammate
column5:
Plan ID: L-2 (wave 0)

Zone: Team
Depends on: Verify the setup on every operating system

In plain words (for beginners)
Before the first real ticket, everybody does one fake ticket from start to finish: Claude Code creates a branch, a tiny file, a pull request, and we close it. This teaches the whole routine with nothing at stake.

What
- Follow the "Practice run" section of docs/ONBOARDING.md with Claude Code.
- Say "go", look at the changes, say "ship it", ask a teammate to review, watch the checks, then CLOSE the pull request without merging.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Each person opened and closed one practice pull request.
- ☐ Each person can explain what "go" and "ship it" mean and what the six checks are.
- ☐ Anything confusing was written down for Nour (feeds the docs).

column2: Invite everyone and complete CODEOWNERS
column5:
Plan ID: L-3 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: nothing (run as soon as each username is known)
Files allowed (optional): .github/CODEOWNERS, docs/TEAM.md, docs/LEAD_SETUP.md

In plain words (for beginners)
CODEOWNERS is a file saying who must approve changes to which folders. Each time a person joins we add their GitHub name, and remove the temporary placeholders.

What
- Invite Lina, Zahraa and Judy as collaborators with Write access (Settings > Collaborators). Confirm each accepted. DONE for all (Eya, Lina, Zahraa, Judy).
- /apps/ has Nour and Lina (done). /templates/ and /static/ have Eya, Zahraa and Judy, with Nour and Lina as backup reviewers (done).
- Add the handles to the table in docs/TEAM.md.
- After merging, open GitHub's CODEOWNERS page for the repo: there must be no errors.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ All five people are collaborators with Write (not Admin).
- ☐ A test pull request touching /templates/ asks for review from the frontend owners (Nour and Lina only as backup).
- ☐ CODEOWNERS shows no errors on GitHub.

column2: GitHub settings round (alerts, required checks, review of the rules)
column5:
Plan ID: L-4 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: Invite everyone and complete CODEOWNERS

In plain words (for beginners)
Some safety settings can only be switched on in the GitHub website. This ticket is the checklist for them.

What
- Settings > Code security: turn on Dependabot alerts (free). DONE 2026-11-11.
- Settings > Rules > Protect main: add the `docker` job next to `checks` under "Require status checks" once it has passed at least 10 times. DONE 2026-11-11.
- Decide whether to remove the admin bypass from the ruleset now that others can approve (if yes: remember your own PRs then need a teammate's approval).
- Confirm the workflow permissions are read-only (Settings > Actions > General).
- Confirm "Automatically delete head branches" and squash-only merging are still on.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Each item done or consciously decided (decision written in docs/DECISIONS.md).

column2: Jira setup (template, workflow, board, rhythm)
column5:
Plan ID: L-5 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead (with Eya, who owns the Jira site)
Depends on: nothing

In plain words (for beginners)
Jira is our to-do board. A little setup makes tickets easy to write and easy to follow.

What
- Description template with the lines: Zone, Files allowed (optional), Contract, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope, Depends on (see docs/LEAD_SETUP.md).
- Columns: To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done. Components: Backend, Frontend, Lead.
- Labels per area: accounts, strains, plasmids, primers, search, import, backup, deploy.
- One sprint per wave (Wave 0, Wave 2, ...), as in `docs/tickets/README.md`. Client demos stay every two weeks, whatever sprint is running.
- Optional: try the GitHub-for-Jira link (Eya installs the app, Nour approves on GitHub); if a personal GitHub account is not supported, skip it.
- A rule everyone follows: move your ticket to In Progress when you start and to In Review when the pull request is open.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ A new ticket created from the template looks right.
- ☐ The board shows the four columns and the components.

column2: Collect the open client questions and record the answers
column5:
Plan ID: L-6 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: nothing

In plain words (for beginners)
Some decisions are not ours: they belong to the client (the lab). We ask them once, in one message, and write the answers down so nobody has to ask again.

What
Send ONE message to the client (Max / Mateusz) with these questions, then record each answer in docs/DECISIONS.md:
1. Primer melting temperature (Tm): which formula should we use?
2. Primer sequences: only A, C, G, T, or also ambiguity letters (N, R, Y, ...)?
3. Should "purpose" (Sequencing, PCR, Cloning, ...) be a fixed list or free text? Which values?
4. Biosafety level: which values do they use (BSL-1, BSL-2, ...)?
5. Backups: answered by the client's e-mail (automatic backups; an admin copies them to another system by hand). Still to ask: how often, how long to keep them, who restores?
6. Import: what format can the Word files be exported to (CSV/Excel)? Can they provide 20-50 anonymised sample records (after asking the professor)? (They already sent excerpts of the three Word files; those stay out of Git.)
7. SnapGene: may we test "click to open" on one lab PC? Is the Hessenbox folder synced on the lab computer that will host the app?
8. Hosting: the group wants its own hardware and suggests a NAS server (bring pros and cons to the next meeting). Which machine (lab computer or NAS), operating system, is it on 24/7, who restarts it, what is its network name?
9. Who may see which data: may students export data? Is any data confidential?
10. Licence and ownership: answered. The client confirmed by e-mail that open source is fine; students keep the rights to their own code (course rules); the team chose AGPL-3.0-or-later (D14).
11. How should demos and change requests be collected (every two weeks)?

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ The message is sent; every answer (or "not decided yet") is in docs/DECISIONS.md.
- ☐ Tickets that were waiting for an answer are updated.

column2: Claude accounts: everyone can use Claude Code
column5:
Plan ID: L-7 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: nothing

In plain words (for beginners)
Claude Code needs a Claude account. Sharing one personal account between several people is probably not allowed, so we need a proper plan.

What
- Check Anthropic's terms for team use; decide the plan (individual subscriptions, a team plan, or API access) and who pays.
- Make sure each teammate can run `claude` and sign in.
- Record the decision in docs/DECISIONS.md.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ All five people can start Claude Code in the project folder.
- ☐ The decision is written down.

column2: Review and trim AGENTS.md after the first week
column5:
Plan ID: L-8 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: Practice run for every teammate (plus about a week of real tickets)
Files allowed (optional): AGENTS.md, docs/PROMPTING_GUIDE.md, docs/SYNC_WITH_MAIN.md

In plain words (for beginners)
AGENTS.md is the rulebook Claude Code follows. It is long. After a week we look at what actually happened and keep only what helps.

What
- Read the docs/ai-log/ files and the closed/merged pull requests. List the rules that were broken, ignored or caused friction.
- Shorten wording, remove rules nobody needs, add rules for real problems.
- Check that all documents still agree with each other.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ AGENTS.md is shorter (target under 300 lines) with no lost safety rule.
- ☐ A list "what we changed and why" is in the pull request.

column2: Bi-weekly client demo and change-request routine
column5:
Plan ID: L-9 (wave 0)

Zone: Lead (recurring ticket, one per demo)
Depends on: nothing

In plain words (for beginners)
The client wants a demo every two weeks. We prepare the same way each time, and every new wish becomes a ticket we can prioritise.

What (each demo)
- Two days before: pick what to show, run it from a fresh clone on one PC (the demo machine), seed fake data (never real data).
- Write a short demo script (5 to 10 steps) and test it once.
- During the demo: one person drives, one person writes down every wish and question.
- After the demo: turn each wish into a Jira ticket labelled "change-request" and ask the client to order them by priority.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Demo ran from a clean setup. Every wish is a ticket or an answered question.

column2: Team working agreements
column5:
Plan ID: L-10 (wave 0)

Zone: Team
Depends on: nothing

In plain words (for beginners)
A few simple team promises prevent waiting around and surprises.

What (agree, then write it in docs/TEAM.md)
- Review turnaround: a pull request gets its first review within one working day.
- Who reviews whom (rotation), so nobody is always waiting for the same person.
- A short daily check-in (chat message: what I did, what I will do, where I am stuck).
- When stuck for more than 30 minutes: ask in the team chat, with the report from the helper menu (option 18).
- Definition of done: tests added, six checks green, ticket moved, documentation updated if behaviour changed.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Everyone agreed; the text is in docs/TEAM.md (lead PR).

column2: Shared view helpers in apps/core (page size, audit fields, messages)
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B1 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend (SHARED: apps/core, announce to the team first)
Depends on: Database schema v1, Roles and permissions
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/ (views mixins, constants, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
Strain pages, plasmid pages and primer pages all need the same boring things: the same page size, "remember who saved this record", "show a success message". We write those ONCE here so the three apps do not each invent their own version.

What
- PAGE_SIZE = 25 constant.
- AuditedFormMixin: on save sets created_by (first save) and updated_by (every save) from request.user.
- A small mixin that adds a success message after create/update/delete (text supplied by each view).
- A base class or mixin combining: login (already global), permission check, pagination, the `page_obj` and `object_list` context names.
- Tests for each helper using a tiny test model inside the tests package.

Contract for others (docstrings)
- How to use each mixin in three lines with an example.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests for each helper; six checks green.
Out of scope: any real entity view.

column2: Primer pages: list, detail, create, edit
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B2 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Shared view helpers, Database schema v1
Files allowed (optional): apps/primers/ (views.py, forms.py, urls.py, tests/)

In plain words (for beginners)
This makes the primers usable in the website. A "view" answers a web address; a "form" checks what a person typed. The pretty pages come from the frontend tickets; here we provide the data and the rules.

What
- URL names primers:list, primers:detail, primers:create, primers:update (delete comes in the delete ticket).
- List: all primers, newest first, 25 per page.
- Detail: the primer, and the plasmids it is linked to (with orientation and position).
- Form (strict): primer_id and sequence required; purpose, freezer_location optional; the sequence is cleaned by the model rules; length and Tm are shown read-only after saving; extra_data is edited later (extra-fields ticket), not here.
- The purpose field offers suggestions from a list defined in ONE place in the form (a datalist), but accepts other text.
- Permissions: viewing needs primers.view_primer, create needs add, edit needs change.

Contract for the frontend (also in the view docstrings)
- list: context `page_obj`, `object_list`, `is_paginated`. Each row: id, primer_id, sequence, purpose, freezer_location, length_bp, melting_temp_tm.
- detail: context `object` (the primer) and `links` (rows with plasmid, orientation, binding_position).
- create/update: context `form`, fields primer_id, sequence, purpose, freezer_location, and `object` on update. Server messages through the messages framework.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests per view: anonymous -> login; permitted user -> 200 with the expected content; user without permission -> 403; the form rejects invalid sequence letters and a duplicate primer_id (any capitalisation); created_by/updated_by are set.
- ☐ Six checks green.
Out of scope: delete, search, templates (frontend tickets).

column2: Plasmid pages: list, detail, create, edit
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B3 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Shared view helpers, Database schema v1
Files allowed (optional): apps/plasmids/ (views.py, forms.py, urls.py, tests/)

In plain words (for beginners)
Same idea as the primer pages, for plasmids (small circles of DNA). A plasmid can have primers and can be carried by strains.

What
- URL names plasmids:list, plasmids:detail, plasmids:create, plasmids:update.
- List: plasmid_name, size_bp, resistance_markers, copy_number.
- Detail: all fields, the primers linked to it (orientation, binding_position), and the strains that carry it.
- Form (strict): plasmid_name required; size_bp a positive whole number when given; copy_number a dropdown (High, Medium, Low, or empty); sequence_file and hessenbox_path are plain text boxes (the SnapGene ticket later makes them clickable); description optional.
- Permissions as in the primer ticket.

Contract for the frontend
- list: `page_obj`, `object_list`. detail: `object`, `primer_links`, `strains`. form: `form` with the field names above.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Same test set as the primer pages (login, permission, content, validation, duplicate names, audit fields).
- ☐ Six checks green.
Out of scope: delete, search, templates.

column2: Strain pages: list, detail, create, edit
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B4 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Shared view helpers, Database schema v1
Files allowed (optional): apps/strains/ (views.py, forms.py, urls.py, tests/)

In plain words (for beginners)
The strain is the heart of the database: a bacterial line with its genetics and where it is stored. A strain can carry plasmids and can descend from another strain (its "parent").

What
- URL names strains:list, strains:detail, strains:create, strains:update.
- List: strain_id, host_organism, genotype (shortened), culturing_temp, culturing_medium, freezer_location.
- Detail: all fields, the plasmids it carries, its parent strain and its child strains.
- Form (strict): strain_id required; culturing_temp a number in a sensible range (set the range in ONE constant); parent_strain a dropdown of other strains that cannot be the strain itself; biosafety_level offers suggestions from a list in one place but accepts other text.
- Permissions as in the other entities.

Contract for the frontend
- list: `page_obj`, `object_list`. detail: `object`, `plasmid_links`, `parent`, `children`. form: `form`.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: the usual set, plus "a strain cannot be its own parent", "a loop of parents is rejected", "a strain without plasmids or parent saves fine".
- ☐ Six checks green.
Out of scope: delete, search, templates.

column2: Link plasmids to strains and primers to plasmids
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B5 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Primer pages, Plasmid pages, Strain pages
Files allowed (optional): apps/strains/, apps/plasmids/ (views, forms, urls, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
A strain carries plasmids; a plasmid binds primers. This ticket lets a person add and remove those connections from a detail page. Remember the rule: a record never has to have links, and removing a link NEVER deletes either record.

What
- On a strain's page: add a plasmid (pick from a list, optional note) and remove a plasmid link. URL names strains:link_plasmid, strains:unlink_plasmid.
- On a plasmid's page: add a primer (pick the primer, orientation, binding position, note) and remove a primer link. URL names plasmids:link_primer, plasmids:unlink_primer.
- The same pair cannot be linked twice (friendly error message, not a crash).
- Needs the change permission of the page's record; unlinking is a POST request with a CSRF token.

Contract for the frontend
- Link forms as `link_form` in the detail page context, with the field names; unlink buttons post to the unlink URL with the link row's id.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: link, duplicate link, unlink, unlinking keeps both records, permissions (student cannot link), the page works for a record with no links.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Delete with a choice (shared helper and all three apps)
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B6 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend (the helper lives in apps/core, a SHARED area: announce first)
Depends on: Link management
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/, apps/strains/, apps/plasmids/, apps/primers/ (views, urls, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
Deleting a record that is connected to others is risky. Decision D8: we always ask. The confirmation page lists what is linked and lets the person choose: delete only this record (its links disappear, the others stay), or also delete the linked records, but only those that are not linked to anything else.

What
- One shared delete view/mixin in apps/core, used by the three apps: URL names primers:delete, plasmids:delete, strains:delete.
- GET shows the confirmation (context below); POST performs the choice, with a CSRF token.
- "Also delete linked records" is offered only for linked records that nothing else is linked to. A plasmid carried by another strain is NEVER deleted by this option.
- Needs the delete permission (Admin only by default).
- A success message says exactly what was deleted.

Contract for the frontend
- Context: `object`, `linked_exclusive` (linked records that nothing else uses), `linked_shared` (linked records that something else also uses), form field `delete_linked` (checkbox).

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: delete only this record keeps the others; also-delete removes only exclusive ones; shared ones stay; no permission -> 403; a record without links deletes simply; nothing else is deleted in any case.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Home dashboard data and the admin approvals page
column5:
Plan ID: W2-B7 (wave 2)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Accounts v1, Strain pages (for the counts)
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/views.py, apps/core/urls.py, apps/accounts/ (views, urls, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
The home page should say something useful: how many records exist, what changed recently, and (for admins) who is waiting for approval. Admins should be able to approve new sign-ups on a normal page without learning the Django admin.

What
- core:home context: counts of strains, plasmids, primers; the 5 most recently changed records of each kind; for users with the permission, `pending_users` (sign-ups waiting).
- accounts:approvals (Admin only): list of pending sign-ups with their signup_note; POST actions approve (with a role dropdown: Student, Staff or Admin) and reject. Approving sets approval_status, is_active, approved_by, approved_at and adds the chosen group.

Contract for the frontend
- Home: `counts` (dict), `recent` (lists), `pending_users` (or empty). Approvals page: `pending_users`, a form with `user_id` and `role`, POST to accounts:approve and accounts:reject.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: counts are right; recent lists are ordered; pending_users only for admins; approve gives the chosen role; reject deactivates; a Student gets 403 on the approvals page.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Browse, create and edit records (parent)
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F-MAIN (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend

In plain words (for beginners)
This is where the lab's data becomes visible and usable: tables to browse, pages to read one record, forms to add and change records, and a clear way to link and delete. You build on what the backend tickets publish (URL names and context variables in the view docstrings). If a variable you need is missing, ask on the backend ticket; never edit apps/.

Sub-tasks (Jira sub-tasks; each its own PR)
  1. W2-F1 Shared list layout (table, empty state, pagination)       (SHARED FILES)
  2. W2-F2 Primer pages: list, detail, form
  3. W2-F3 Plasmid pages: list, detail, form
  4. W2-F4 Strain pages: list, detail (with lineage), form
  5. W2-F5 Link management on the detail pages
  6. W2-F6 Delete confirmation page
  7. W2-F7 Home dashboard
  8. W2-F8 Admin approvals page
  9. W2-F9 Permission-aware buttons and final polish

Definition of done for the parent
A Staff user can find, read, create, edit and link records; a Student can only read and sees no edit buttons; an Admin can delete with a clear choice; every page has loading-free empty, error and success states.

Things to take care of (apply to every sub-task)
- Everything from the F-MAIN checklist of wave 1 still applies (plain CSS, no CDN, no inline styles, CSRF, labels, no-JS, keyboard, English only).
- Tables: real <table> with header cells (scope="col"), sensible column widths, long text (genotype, sequence) shortened with the full text on the detail page.
- DNA sequences use the monospace style and may wrap anywhere.
- Never show a button the user may not use (check the permissions the backend provides, e.g. \{% if perms.strains.change_strain %\}).
- Links between records are real links (deep links), keyboard reachable.
- Show friendly empty states ("No primers yet") and a "Create" button only for those allowed.
- Every PR: screenshots (list, detail, form, an error state) and the browser checklist.

column2: Shared list layout: table, empty state, pagination
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F1 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend (SHARED FILES: announce first)
Depends on: Design foundation, Form and feedback components
Files allowed (optional): templates/components/, static/css/base.css

In plain words (for beginners)
All three list pages (strains, plasmids, primers) look alike: a title, a button, a table, page numbers. Build that frame once as components.

What
- components/page_header.html (title + optional action button), components/table.html pattern or CSS (zebra rows, hover, sticky header if easy), components/empty_state.html, components/pagination.html using `page_obj`.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Used by the first list page that follows; states: normal, empty, one page, many pages.
- ☐ Browser checklist, screenshot.

column2: Primer pages: list, detail, form
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F2 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Primer pages (backend), Shared list layout
Files allowed (optional): templates/primers/, static/css/pages/primers-*.css

In plain words (for beginners)
The primer is a short piece of DNA, written as a row of letters. Show the letters in a monospace font so they line up and are easy to read.

What
- list.html: columns primer_id (link to detail), sequence (monospace, shortened), purpose, length, Tm, freezer location.
- detail.html: all fields, the linked plasmids (links to their pages with orientation and position), Edit button for those who may.
- form.html: the form using the shared components; help text under sequence ("letters A, C, G, T; 5'- and -3' are removed automatically"); read-only length and Tm shown after saving.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ States: empty list, one page/many pages, a primer with no links, validation errors, success message, permission-less view (no buttons).

column2: Plasmid pages: list, detail, form
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F3 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Plasmid pages (backend), Shared list layout
Files allowed (optional): templates/plasmids/, static/css/pages/plasmids-*.css

What
- list.html: plasmid_name (link), size_bp, resistance_markers, copy_number.
- detail.html: all fields; two sections "Primers" (orientation and position) and "Carried by strains"; sequence_file and hessenbox_path shown as plain text for now (becomes a button later).
- form.html: shared components; copy_number dropdown; size_bp number input with a min value.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Same states as the primer pages, plus a plasmid with no primers and no strains.

column2: Strain pages: list, detail with lineage, form
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F4 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Strain pages (backend), Shared list layout
Files allowed (optional): templates/strains/, static/css/pages/strains-*.css

In plain words (for beginners)
"Lineage" means where a strain came from: its parent, and the strains made from it. Show it simply as two small lists with links.

What
- list.html: strain_id (link), host_organism, genotype (shortened), culturing temperature (with the unit °C), medium, freezer location.
- detail.html: all fields; sections "Plasmids" (links), "Parent strain" (link or "none") and "Child strains" (links).
- form.html: shared components; temperature input with step 0.1; parent dropdown with a clear "none" option.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ States: empty, validation errors, a strain with no plasmids and no parent, a strain with several plasmids and children.

column2: Link management on the detail pages
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F5 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Link management (backend), Strain pages, Plasmid pages (frontend)
Files allowed (optional): templates/strains/, templates/plasmids/, templates/components/link_form.html, static/css/pages/*-links.css

In plain words (for beginners)
On a strain page you add or remove the plasmids it carries; on a plasmid page you add or remove its primers. Removing a link only removes the connection, never the records, and the page must say so.

What
- Small "add" form (a dropdown plus optional fields) and a "remove" button per row (a POST form with a CSRF token) on the two detail pages, shown only to users who may change the record.
- Clear wording under remove: "This only removes the link. Both records stay."
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ States: no links, many links, duplicate-link error, success message, a read-only user sees no add/remove controls.

column2: Delete confirmation page
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F6 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Delete with a choice (backend)
Files allowed (optional): templates/core/confirm_delete.html (or per-app folders), static/css/pages/delete.css

In plain words (for beginners)
Deleting is permanent, so the page must be calm and clear. It names the record, lists what is linked to it, and offers the choice from decision D8.

What
- A page showing the record, the linked records that nothing else uses (can be deleted too) and the linked records others still use (will stay).
- A checkbox "Also delete the linked records that nothing else uses" (unchecked by default), a red Delete button, and a Cancel link back to the record.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ States: no links; only exclusive links; shared links; the cancel path; keyboard use.

column2: Home dashboard
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F7 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Dashboard data and admin approvals page (backend), Design foundation
Files allowed (optional): templates/core/home.html, static/css/pages/core-home.css

What
- Three count cards (Strains, Plasmids, Primers) linking to the lists; "Recently changed" lists; for admins a "N people are waiting for approval" notice linking to the approvals page.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ States: empty database, normal, admin with pending users, student view.

column2: Admin approvals page
column5:
Plan ID: W2-F8 (wave 2)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Dashboard data and admin approvals page (backend)
Files allowed (optional): templates/accounts/approvals.html, static/css/pages/accounts-approvals.css

What
- A table of pending sign-ups (name, username, email, note, date) with a role dropdown and Approve and Reject buttons per row (POST forms with CSRF).
- Empty state "Nobody is waiting".
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ States: empty, one pending, many pending; success and error messages; only admins can open it (403 page otherwise).

column2: Permission-aware buttons and final polish of wave 2
column5:

column2: Search and filter methods for primers, plasmids and strains
column5:
Plan ID: W3-B1 (wave 3)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Primer pages, Plasmid pages, Strain pages
Files allowed (optional): apps/primers/, apps/plasmids/, apps/strains/ (models/querysets, forms, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
A "queryset" is Django's way of asking the database a question. We write the questions ("find primers whose name or sequence contains this text") once, as methods with clear names, and the views simply call them. That keeps the pages short and the rules in one place.

What
- Per entity a queryset method `search(text)`: case-insensitive "contains" on the main text fields
  - primers: primer_id, purpose, sequence, freezer_location
  - plasmids: plasmid_name, resistance_markers, description
  - strains: strain_id, host_organism, genotype, freezer_location
  Several words mean ALL words must match (AND). A word may match in any of the fields.
- Per entity filter methods, one per filter, each ignoring an empty value:
  - primers: purpose, has_plasmid (yes/no)
  - plasmids: resistance marker, copy number, size range (min/max)
  - strains: host organism, biosafety level, culturing temperature range, plasmid (strain carries plasmid X), parent strain
- A FilterForm per entity (Django form, not required fields) that validates the GET parameters and returns the filtered queryset.
- Wrong input (letters in a size box) shows a form error and is ignored, it never crashes the page.

Contract for the frontend (view docstrings)
- Parameters: `q`, the filter names above, `sort`, `page`.
- Context: `filter_form` (fields to render), `result_count`, `active_filters` (list of label + value + the address that removes it).

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests for every search field and every filter, empty input, wrong input, multi-word search, capital letters.
- ☐ A test with 3 records shows that only the right ones come back.
- ☐ Six checks green.
Out of scope: templates, JavaScript, global search.

column2: Sorting and pagination that keep search and filters
column5:
Plan ID: W3-B2 (wave 3)

Zone: Backend (the helper lives in apps/core: SHARED, announce first)
Depends on: Search and filter methods
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/, the three list views, tests

In plain words (for beginners)
If you search for "pET", go to page 2 and the search disappears, that is a bug. Also people want to click a column title to sort. This ticket makes page numbers and sorting remember the search.

What
- A shared helper that takes the current GET parameters and builds new addresses: "page 3", "sort by size", "remove this filter" (always keeping the other parameters).
- Allowed sort columns are a fixed list per entity (a whitelist). Any other `sort` value is ignored (safety: never pass raw text to the database).
- Default sort: newest first (or by name, decide once and write it in the docstring).
- Context for the frontend: `querystring_without_page`, `sort_links` (column -> address, current direction).

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: page 2 keeps `q` and filters; unknown sort ignored; descending sort works; going out of range gives the last page, not an error.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Global search page across strains, plasmids and primers
column5:
Plan ID: W3-B3 (wave 3)

Zone: Backend (SHARED: apps/core, announce to the other backend dev first)
Depends on: Search and filter methods
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/views.py, apps/core/urls.py, apps/core/tests/

In plain words (for beginners)
A person looking for "pUC19" often does not know whether it is a plasmid or the name inside a strain. One search box in the top bar searches everything and shows results grouped by kind.

What
- URL name `core:search`, parameter `q`. Uses the three `search()` methods (never new query code here).
- At most 10 results per kind, with a "see all N" address into the full list page with the same `q`.
- Needs the view permission of each kind: kinds the user may not view are skipped.
- Fewer than 2 characters: no search, a friendly hint.

Contract for the frontend
- Context: `q`, `results` = list of groups (kind label, items, total, list_url), `too_short`.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: results grouped correctly; empty and short search; a user without a permission does not see that group; capital letters.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Live search JSON endpoint
column5:
Plan ID: W3-B4 (wave 3)

Zone: Backend (SHARED: apps/core, announce to the other backend dev first)
Depends on: Global search page
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/api.py, apps/core/urls.py, apps/core/tests/

In plain words (for beginners)
"Live search" shows suggestions while you type, without reloading the page. The browser asks a small web address and gets JSON back (JSON is just structured text a program can read). This ticket builds that address; the frontend ticket builds the typing box.

What
- URL name `core:search_api`, GET only, parameter `q`, login required like everything else.
- Returns JSON with the SAME grouping rules as the global search but small: at most 5 results per kind.
- Uses Django's JsonResponse. Never build JSON by hand.
- Wrong or empty input returns an empty result, never an error page.

Contract for the frontend (this exact shape, also in the docstring)
  \{ "q": "puc",
    "groups": \[
      \{ "kind": "plasmid", "label": "Plasmids", "total": 12,
        "items": \[ \{ "id": 7, "title": "pUC19", "subtitle": "2686 bp, AmpR", "url": "/plasmids/7/" \} \] \}
    \] \}

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: shape is exactly as above; anonymous request is redirected or refused (never data); permission skipping; at most 5 per kind.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Search performance: indexes and query count
column5:
Plan ID: W3-B5 (wave 3)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Search and filter methods, Global search page
Files allowed (optional): apps/*/models.py (Meta indexes), apps/*/migrations/ (follow the migration rules!), apps/*/tests/, apps/core/management/commands/

In plain words (for beginners)
With 50 records everything is fast. With 5000 it can become slow if the database has to look at every row. An "index" is like the index of a book: it lets the database jump straight to the answer. We measure first, then add only the indexes we need.

What
- Extend the fake data command with a bigger size (for example `--size large`: 5000 strains, 2000 plasmids, 5000 primers, with links). Development only.
- Add tests that assert the number of database queries on each list page and the detail pages (use `assertNumQueries`), fixing N+1 problems with select_related / prefetch_related.
- Measure the search with the large data set. If a search takes longer than 200 ms, add the indexes (or trigram indexes with the Postgres pg_trgm extension, which needs a lead-approved migration step) and show before/after numbers in the pull request.
- Follow the migration rules: one open migration pull request for the app, never edit a merged migration.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Query counts are fixed and tested (do not grow with the number of rows).
- ☐ Before/after timings in the pull request.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Search and filter experience (parent)
column5:
Plan ID: W3-F-MAIN (wave 3)

Zone: Frontend

In plain words (for beginners)
This is the feature the lab will use every day: type a few letters, find the strain. It must feel fast, clear and forgiving. You build on the backend contract (parameters and context variables in the view docstrings).

Sub-tasks
  1. W3-F1 Search bar component in the top bar                  (SHARED FILES)
  2. W3-F2 Filter panel component and per-entity filter layouts
  3. W3-F3 Sortable column headers and active-filter chips
  4. W3-F4 Global search results page
  5. W3-F5 Live search dropdown (JavaScript)
  6. W3-F6 Search states: empty, loading, error, too short, no results

Definition of done for the parent
From any page a person can search, open a result, narrow a list with filters, share the address of the result, and everything still works without JavaScript.

Things to take care of
- Search is a normal <form method="get">; JavaScript only adds speed.
- Keep what the user typed in the box after searching; show the number of results.
- Labels for every input; the search input has type="search" and an accessible name.
- Matches may be highlighted with the <mark> element (done in the template filter, never with innerHTML on user text).
- All earlier frontend rules apply (plain CSS, no CDN, no inline styles, keyboard use, English only).

column2: Search bar component in the top bar

Files allowed (optional): templates/components/search_bar.html, templates/base.html (nav part only), static/css/base.css

column2: Sortable column headers and active-filter chips
column5:

column2: Global search results page
column5:
Plan ID: W3-F4 (wave 3)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Global search page (backend), Search bar component
Files allowed (optional): templates/core/search.html, static/css/pages/core-search.css

What
- Groups with headings (Strains, Plasmids, Primers), each result a link with title and subtitle, a "see all N" link per group, the count of results, the typed text kept in the box.

column2: Live search dropdown while typing
column5:
Plan ID: W3-F5 (wave 3)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Live search JSON endpoint (backend), Search bar component
Files allowed (optional): static/js/pages/core-live-search.js, static/css/pages/core-live-search.css, templates/components/search_bar.html (SHARED: announce first)

In plain words (for beginners)
While the user types, a small box under the input shows the best matches. JavaScript sends the text to the JSON address and draws the answer. "Debounce" means waiting about 250 ms after the last key so we do not ask the server on every single letter.

What
- Plain JavaScript file (no libraries, no CDN). Debounce 250 ms; cancel the previous request when a new one starts (AbortController).
- Draw results with textContent (never innerHTML with user text, to avoid XSS).
- Accessibility: role="listbox"/"option" or a simple list with aria-live="polite" announcing "N results"; arrow keys move, Enter opens, Escape closes; focus never trapped.
- If JavaScript fails or the address errors: the normal form submit still works and a short message appears.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Works with the mouse and keyboard only; slow network and error states checked (browser dev tools "Slow 3G", offline).
- ☐ No console errors; the page works with JavaScript disabled.

column2: Search states: empty, loading, error, too short
column5:
Plan ID: W3-F6 (wave 3)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Live search dropdown, Global search results page

What

- Loading indicator in plain CSS (no GIF); respects "reduce motion".
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Screenshot of each state; the same component used everywhere.

column2: SnapGene spike: can the browser open a .dna file on a lab PC?
column5:
Plan ID: W4-L1 (wave 4)

Zone: Lead (with the client)
Depends on: client answers to the SnapGene and Hessenbox questions (ticket L-6)

In plain words (for beginners)
SnapGene is the program biologists use to look at plasmid maps. The client wants one click in our website to open a plasmid file in SnapGene. Browsers are strict about opening local programs, so we first TRY the possible ways on a real lab PC before anyone builds anything. A "spike" is a short experiment that ends with a decision, not with finished code.

What
Try on one lab PC (Windows, SnapGene installed, Hessenbox folder synced) and write down what works:
1. Plain download: the website serves the .dna file as a download; the browser opens it with SnapGene (file type association).
2. A link to the synced file path (file:// links are usually blocked from web pages: confirm).
3. A custom link scheme if SnapGene offers one (check SnapGene documentation).
4. A link to the file in the Hessenbox/Nextcloud web page.
Record per option: works yes/no, number of clicks, what the user sees, any security warning.

Output
- Decision in docs/DECISIONS.md (lead pull request): which option we build, and what the database must store (a path relative to a folder, or a full link).
- The hessenbox_path field format (what a valid value looks like) is written into docs/DOMAIN.md.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tested on at least one real lab PC with the client's help.
- ☐ A decision is written; W4-B1 and W4-F1 can be updated with it.

column2: Serve or link plasmid files so SnapGene can open them
column5:
Plan ID: W4-B1 (wave 4)

Zone: Backend (the mounted folder in docker-compose.yml is a LEAD change: see W4-L2)
Depends on: SnapGene spike (decision), Plasmid pages (backend)
Files allowed (optional): apps/plasmids/ (views, urls, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
Depending on the spike's decision, either (a) our server hands the .dna file to the browser as a download, or (b) the page just shows a link. This ticket is written for option (a), the most likely one; adjust it after the spike.

What (option a)
- URL name `plasmids:snapgene_file` (GET only, login required, permission plasmids.view_plasmid).
- Reads the file named by the plasmid's `sequence_file`/`hessenbox_path` from ONE configured base folder (setting name defined by the lead in W4-L2). Nothing outside that folder can ever be read:
  - reject absolute paths, `..`, and symbolic links that leave the folder;
  - only allow the extensions the client uses (.dna, .gb, .fa ...), defined once as a constant.
- Sends the file with Django's FileResponse as an attachment with a safe file name; a missing file shows a friendly 404 page, not a crash.
- Never logs file contents.

Contract for the frontend
- Plasmid detail context gets `snapgene_url` (the address above) or None when the plasmid has no file.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: file served for a valid name; `../` and absolute path rejected; missing file -> 404; no permission -> 403; no file set -> `snapgene_url` is None.
- ☐ Reviewer guide in the pull request names the path-safety code as the place needing most attention.
- ☐ Six checks green.
Out of scope: Docker volume, template.

column2: Sequence helper functions: reverse complement, GC content, cleaning
column5:
Plan ID: W4-B2 (wave 4)

Zone: Backend (SHARED: apps/core, announce first)
Depends on: Database schema v1 (and the client's answer about Tm formula and allowed letters, for the two marked items)
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/sequence.py, apps/core/tests/test_sequence.py

In plain words (for beginners)
DNA is written as a string of the letters A, C, G and T. Biologists constantly need small calculations on those strings. We write them as plain Python functions with clear tests, once, so models, forms and pages all use the same ones.

What (each a small, pure function with a docstring)
- clean_sequence(text): uppercase, remove spaces/newlines/digits, remove 5'- and -3' markers; raise a clear error for letters that are not allowed.
- reverse_complement(seq): A<->T, C<->G, reversed.
- gc_content(seq): percentage of G and C (rounded to 1 decimal).
- melting_temperature(seq): ONLY after the client confirms the formula (a function with the chosen formula named in its docstring).
- format_blocks(seq, size=10): "ACGTACGTAC GTACGTACGT ..." for display.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Unit tests with hand-checked values (write the calculation in a comment next to each test); wrong letters raise the expected error; empty input handled.
- ☐ The existing models/forms are NOT changed in this ticket (a follow-up small ticket switches them to these helpers if they have their own copies).
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Warn about duplicate IDs and duplicate sequences when saving
column5:
Plan ID: W4-B3 (wave 4)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Primer pages, Plasmid pages, Strain pages, Sequence helpers
Files allowed (optional): apps/primers/forms.py, apps/plasmids/forms.py, apps/strains/forms.py, tests

In plain words (for beginners)
Two people entering the same primer twice is the most common data problem in a lab database. Identical IDs are already blocked (that is a hard rule, any capitalisation). Two DIFFERENT IDs with the SAME sequence is allowed but suspicious, so we show a warning with a link to the existing record and let the person continue.

What
- On the primer form: if another primer has the same cleaned sequence, show a non-blocking warning ("Primer P-017 has the same sequence") naming the records, with links.
- The user can still save (an explicit tick box "Save anyway").
- Same idea for plasmids with the same name ignoring spaces and capitals ("pUC19" vs "puc 19").
Contract for the frontend
- Form context: `duplicate_warnings` (list of: message, record label, record url) and the field `confirm_duplicate`.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: warning shown, can save with confirmation, cannot save without it, no warning for unique data, own record not counted when editing.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Strain lineage: ancestors and descendants
column5:
Plan ID: W4-B4 (wave 4)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Strain pages (backend)
Files allowed (optional): apps/strains/ (models methods, views, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
"Lineage" is the family tree of a strain: its parent, grandparent, and so on, and the strains made from it. The strain page already shows the direct parent and children; this ticket adds the full chain, safely (a data mistake must never freeze the page in an endless loop).

What
- Methods `ancestors()` and `descendants()` (lists, with the depth number), written with a loop and a visited-set so a cycle in bad data stops cleanly; limit depth to 20.
- Detail view context: `ancestors` (nearest first) and `descendants` (tree order with depth).
- No new database columns (uses the existing parent link).
Contract for the frontend
- `ancestors`: list of \{strain, depth\}. `descendants`: list of \{strain, depth\}.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: chain of 3, branching children, no parent/no children, a deliberate loop does not hang, query count stays small (use assertNumQueries).
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Suggestion lists for free-text fields (host organism, medium, location, markers)
column5:
Plan ID: W4-B5 (wave 4)

Zone: Backend (the helper in apps/core is SHARED: announce first)
Depends on: Strain pages, Plasmid pages, Primer pages
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/, apps/strains/forms.py, apps/plasmids/forms.py, apps/primers/forms.py, tests

In plain words (for beginners)
Fields like "host organism" are free text (so scientists are never blocked), but typing "E.coli", "E. coli" and "Escherichia coli" for the same thing makes searching messy. A suggestion list (an HTML <datalist>) offers the values already used, so people usually pick an existing one. This is decision D-permissive-database + strict-forms in practice: we guide, we do not block.

What
- One shared helper that returns the distinct existing values of a field, most used first, limited to 50.
- Used by the forms for: host_organism, culturing_medium, biosafety_level, freezer_location (strains/primers), resistance_markers (plasmids), purpose (primers, together with the fixed starter list from the client).
- The form exposes them as `suggestions` for each field.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: ordering by use, empty database gives an empty list, a value typed outside the list still saves.
- ☐ Query count tested (one query per field at most).
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Mount the Hessenbox/SnapGene folder into the web container (read-only)
column5:
Plan ID: W4-L2 (wave 4)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: SnapGene spike (decision)
Files allowed (optional): docker-compose.yml, .env.example, config/settings/base.py, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/ONBOARDING.md

In plain words (for beginners)
The website runs inside a Docker container that cannot see the computer's folders unless we say so. We "mount" the plasmid-file folder into the container as read-only, so the website can read the files but can never change or delete them.

What
- A volume in docker-compose.yml mapping a host folder (from an environment variable, default an empty example folder inside the repo's data/ that is git-ignored) to a fixed path in the container, mounted read-only.
- A setting (for example PLASMID_FILES_ROOT) read from the environment, documented in .env.example.
- ONBOARDING note: developers do NOT need the real folder; the default example folder is enough.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ `docker compose up` still works for everybody without extra steps (no real folder needed).
- ☐ The container cannot write into the folder (try `touch` inside, it fails).

column2: Lab features on the pages (parent)
column5:
Plan ID: W4-F-MAIN (wave 4)

Zone: Frontend

In plain words (for beginners)
These pieces make the pages feel made for biologists: reading sequences comfortably, opening SnapGene with a click, seeing the family tree of a strain, and getting gentle hints while typing.

Sub-tasks

  2. W4-F2 Sequence display component (blocks, copy button, counts)

Definition of done for the parent
A biologist can open a plasmid in SnapGene from its page, read and copy a sequence without errors, understand a strain's family tree at a glance, and is warned before creating a duplicate.

Things to take care of

- DNA letters use the monospace tokens from the design foundation; the optional colouring of A/C/G/T must not rely on colour alone and must keep readable contrast.

column5:
Plan ID: W4-F1 (wave 4)

column2: Sequence display component: blocks, copy button, counts
column5:
Plan ID: W4-F2 (wave 4)

Depends on: Sequence helpers (backend), Design foundation

Long DNA strings are hard to read. We show them in groups of 10 letters, with the length, and a "Copy" button.

What
- components/sequence.html used with `\{% include "components/sequence.html" with sequence=... %\}`: monospace, grouped by 10 (the backend helper `format_blocks`, passed in or a template filter owned by backend), line numbers every 60 letters on long sequences, length shown.

column2: Lineage section on the strain page
column5:
Plan ID: W4-F3 (wave 4)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Strain lineage data (backend), Strain pages (frontend)
Files allowed (optional): templates/strains/ (detail or a new partial), static/css/pages/strains-lineage.css

In plain words (for beginners)
Show the family tree as an indented list: ancestors above the strain (oldest first), then the strain highlighted, then its descendants indented by depth. Each name is a link.

What
- Indentation by `depth` using CSS classes (no inline style).

column2: Duplicate warnings and suggestion lists in the forms
column5:
Plan ID: W4-F4 (wave 4)

Depends on: Duplicate warnings (backend), Suggestion lists (backend), Form and feedback components
Files allowed (optional): templates/primers/form.html, templates/plasmids/form.html, templates/strains/form.html, templates/components/form_field.html (SHARED: announce first if it needs a change), static/css/pages/*

column2: Live sequence tools on the primer form
column5:
Plan ID: W4-F5 (wave 4)

Zone: Frontend
Depends on: Primer pages (frontend), Sequence display component
Files allowed (optional): static/js/pages/primers-form.js, templates/primers/form.html, static/css/pages/primers-form.css

In plain words (for beginners)
While the person types a primer, show instantly: how long it is, the GC percentage, and the reverse complement. This is only a convenience: the server recalculates and validates everything when saving (the numbers shown are never trusted by the server).

What
- Plain JavaScript that reads the sequence box and updates three small read-only outputs (use textContent). Invalid letters are highlighted with text, not only colour.
- The formulas are written once in the JS file with a comment pointing to the Python helper they mirror; a short test list of 3 example sequences with expected results goes in the pull request (no automated JS tests, decision D9).
- No melting temperature in JavaScript; Tm appears only after saving (server value).
Acceptance criteria

column2: Backups: schedule, storage, retention and a restore drill
column5:
Plan ID: W5-L1 (wave 5)

Zone: Lead
Depends on: client answers about backups (ticket L-6, question 5), Management commands to back up and restore the database
Files allowed (optional): docker-compose.yml, tools/, docs/BACKUP.md (new), docs/DECISIONS.md, .env.example

In plain words (for beginners)
A backup is a copy of the whole database kept somewhere else. The rule of thumb: a backup you have never restored is only a hope. So this ticket ends with a REAL restore test on a clean machine.

What
- Decide with the client: how often (suggestion: every night), how long we keep them (suggestion: 14 daily + 12 monthly). The client has already decided the rest: the backup runs automatically on the server, and an admin copies it to another system by hand.
- A script in tools/ (works on the lab PC: Windows with Docker) that calls the backup command from W5-B3, names the file with the date, writes it to the backup folder on the server and deletes old ones by the retention rule.
- A scheduled task (Windows Task Scheduler, or cron on Linux) that runs it, with the exact steps in docs/BACKUP.md and a screenshot checklist for the person who sets it up.
- docs/BACKUP.md: how to restore, step by step, with copy-paste commands, for someone who has never done it. It also describes the admin's manual copy to another system: who does it, how often, and how to check it worked.
- THE RESTORE DRILL: on a different computer, take last night's backup, restore it, log in, and check that the record counts match. Write the date and result in docs/BACKUP.md.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ A backup runs by itself at the scheduled time and appears in the server's backup folder; the manual copy to another system is documented and was done once in the drill.
- ☐ Old backups are removed by the retention rule (tested with fake dates).
- ☐ The restore drill succeeded and is recorded.
- ☐ Failure is noticed: the script writes a log and the checklist says who looks at it weekly.

column2: Import command for strains, plasmids and primers (CSV)
column5:
Plan ID: W5-B1 (wave 5)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Database schema v1, Agree the import format with the client and write it down, Sequence helper functions: reverse complement, GC content, cleaning
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/management/commands/import_data.py (SHARED: announce first), apps/core/importing.py, apps/core/tests/, apps/core/tests/fixtures/

In plain words (for beginners)
The lab's data is in Word tables today. Somebody exports them to CSV (a plain text table that Excel and Python both read). This command reads the CSV files and creates the records, and the links between them. It must be safe to run twice: running it again updates existing records instead of making duplicates.

What
- `python manage.py import_data --strains strains.csv --plasmids plasmids.csv --primers primers.csv \[--dry-run\]`
- Each row is validated with the SAME form/model rules as the website (never a second set of rules): wrong rows are collected into a report, good rows are still imported (unless `--strict`, which imports nothing when any row is wrong).
- Match existing records by their ID (case-insensitive): found = update, not found = create. Counts of created / updated / skipped are printed.
- Links by ID columns (for example a strain row lists its plasmid names separated by `;`; a plasmid row lists primers with orientation). A link to an ID that does not exist is a reported error, not a crash and not a silently created empty record.
- The whole import runs in one database transaction: a crash halfway leaves nothing half-imported.
- `--dry-run`: does everything, rolls back, prints the report.
- The report: a text file next to the input (`import-report-<date>.txt`) listing row number, ID, and the problem in plain English.
- Sets created_by/updated_by to a configured "import" user (created if missing), so it is visible in the audit fields.
- UTF-8 (with or without BOM) and both comma and semicolon separators (Excel in Germany uses semicolons).

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests with small FAKE CSV files: clean import; dry-run changes nothing; re-import updates not duplicates; bad rows reported; unknown link target reported; transaction rolls back on failure; semicolon file; BOM file; capital letters in IDs.
- ☐ No real data in the repository.
- ☐ Six checks green.
Out of scope: web upload page, Word (.docx) parsing.

column2: Export lists as CSV and everything as one download
column5:
Plan ID: W5-B2 (wave 5)

Zone: Backend (shared helper in apps/core: announce first)
Depends on: Search and filter methods (wave 3), Roles and permissions
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/export.py, apps/strains/views.py, apps/plasmids/views.py, apps/primers/views.py, apps/strains/urls.py, apps/plasmids/urls.py, apps/primers/urls.py, tests

In plain words (for beginners)
People want their data out: for a paper, for Excel, for safety. Two things: (1) "download this list as CSV", respecting the current search and filters, and (2) one button for admins that downloads everything.

What
- `<app>:export_csv` (GET): the CURRENT filtered list as CSV, all rows (not just page 1), UTF-8 with BOM (so German Excel shows umlauts correctly), semicolon-safe quoting. Columns = the list columns plus all fields and the audit dates. `extra_data` is written as one JSON text column.
- `core:export_all` (GET, admins only, permission-based): a zip with the three CSV files plus a JSON dump with all the links.
- Needs a specific permission (for example `strains.export_strain`); whether Students get it is a client question (L-6 question 9). Default: staff and admin only.
- Uses streaming (StreamingHttpResponse) so a big table does not fill memory.
- Cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are prefixed with an apostrophe (protects Excel users from formula injection).

Contract for the frontend
- Context on list pages: `export_url` (with the current query string) or None when not allowed.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: filtered export contains only the matches; permission check; BOM present; formula-injection cells escaped; zip contains the expected files; JSON links correct.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Management commands to back up and restore the database
column5:
Plan ID: W5-B3 (wave 5)

Zone: Backend (command in apps/core: SHARED, announce first)
Depends on: Database schema v1
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/management/commands/backup_db.py, apps/core/management/commands/restore_db.py, apps/core/tests/

In plain words (for beginners)
These are the two buttons the lead's script (W5-L1) presses. A command is a program you run with `python manage.py <name>`. `pg_dump` is PostgreSQL's own tool that writes the database to a file; we just call it correctly and safely.

What
- `backup_db --output <folder>`: runs pg_dump (custom format, compressed) using the database settings, writes `strain-db-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.dump`, prints the file name and size, exits with an error code if anything failed. The database password is passed through the environment, NEVER on the command line and never printed.
- `restore_db <file> --yes-really`: refuses to run without the flag, and refuses when DEBUG is off unless a second flag `--production` is given; shows what database it will overwrite and asks to type its name.
- The Docker image must contain the postgres client tools (this needs a Dockerfile change: a LEAD ticket W5-L3; until then tests mock the subprocess).
- Tests mock the subprocess and assert the exact command line; one slow test (marked) runs a real dump and restore only when pg_dump exists.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: arguments, file naming, failure exit code, password not in the printed output, restore refuses without the flags.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Extra fields: definitions and forms for the flexible columns (extra_data)
column5:
Plan ID: W5-B4 (wave 5)

Zone: Backend (new model = migration: follow the migration rules)
Depends on: Database schema v1, Strain/Plasmid/Primer pages, decision D6
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/ (SHARED: models, forms), apps/*/forms.py, apps/*/migrations/ (ONE app's migration only), tests

In plain words (for beginners)
The client said "we want the database to be flexible in the columns". Every record has an `extra_data` box (JSON) for extra attributes. But a JSON box is useless if nobody knows which keys exist or what they mean. So admins DEFINE extra fields ("Gel band size", a number, for primers) and the forms then show them as normal inputs. No new database column is ever needed.

What
- A model `ExtraFieldDefinition`: applies_to (strain / plasmid / primer), key (short, letters/digits/underscore, unique per kind, never changed after creation), label, type (text, number, yes/no, date, one-of-list), choices (for one-of-list), required (False by default), help_text, order, active. Follows the project model rules (audited, no `choices=` on growing lists).
- Forms: for each active definition of the kind, add a field to the create/edit form and store the value under `extra_data\[key\]`. Existing records without the key stay valid.
- Deactivating a definition hides the field but NEVER deletes stored values.
- Validation by the field type; wrong value -> a normal form error.
- Admin screen to manage the definitions (Django admin is fine for version 1).

Contract for the frontend
- Forms: extra fields appear as ordinary `form` fields named `extra__<key>`, in order, after the fixed fields. Detail pages get `extra_values` (list of label + value).

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: each type validates; saving stores the key; editing a record without the key works; deactivate hides but keeps; duplicate key rejected; key format enforced.
- ☐ Exactly one new migration file, in ONE app, announced to the other backend developer first.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Change history: who changed what and when
column5:
Plan ID: W5-B5 (wave 5)

Zone: Backend (migration: follow the migration rules)
Depends on: Strain/Plasmid/Primer pages, Delete with a choice
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/ (SHARED: model, signals or mixin, views, tests), apps/core/migrations/

In plain words (for beginners)
The created_by / updated_by columns tell you who touched a record LAST. A change history keeps EVERY change: "Anna changed freezer location from F2 to F5 on 3 May". Labs need this when something goes missing or a value looks wrong. We write it ourselves in a few lines (no extra package, per the project rules).

What
- A model `ChangeLogEntry`: what kind of record, its id, a text label (so it stays readable after deletion), who, when, action (created / changed / deleted / linked / unlinked) and a small JSON with the changed fields \{name: \[old, new\]\}. Never stores passwords or personal data beyond the username.
- Recorded in the shared view mixins (create/update/delete/link views), not with hidden magic, so it is easy to read and to test. Import and the Django admin are covered too (document how).
- A page `core:history` (admins and staff): newest first, filter by record kind, user and date, paginated.
- A per-record "History" section on the detail page context: `history` (last 20 entries).
- Entries are never editable or deletable through the website.

Contract for the frontend
- `history_entries`: list of \{when, who, action, summary, changes\}. The summary text is built by the backend in English.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: create/update/delete/link each produce one entry with the right fields; unchanged save produces none; deleted record's history survives; no secrets in entries; permissions.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Data quality report: find records that need attention
column5:
Plan ID: W5-B6 (wave 5)

Zone: Backend
Depends on: Strain/Plasmid/Primer pages, Sequence helpers
Files allowed (optional): apps/core/ (SHARED: view, checks module, tests)

In plain words (for beginners)
After importing old Word data there will be gaps and oddities. This page lists them so the lab can clean up: it is a to-do list for the data, not an error screen.

What
- URL name `core:data_quality`, for users with the change permission. Sections, each with a count and links to the records:
  - primers without a freezer location; plasmids without a size; strains without a host organism;
  - primers whose stored length or Tm does not match the sequence (should be impossible, but import can bypass forms);
  - sequences with letters that are not allowed;
  - records that are not linked to anything (informational only, since standalone records are allowed);
  - possible duplicates (same sequence, or same name ignoring spaces and capitals).
- Every check is a small function in one module, easy to add to.
- Read-only: it never changes data.

Contract for the frontend
- `sections`: list of \{title, description, count, items (record label + url)\}.

Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Tests: each check finds its planted case and ignores clean records; a user without permission gets 403.
- ☐ Six checks green.

column2: Security review of the project and fix list
column5:
Plan ID: W6-B2 (wave 6)

Zone: Backend (review) with the lead (config changes are lead-only)
Depends on: waves 2 and 3 merged
Files allowed (optional): none for the review itself; findings become tickets

In plain words (for beginners)
We check the usual web mistakes one by one. Each check below has an expected answer; anything different becomes a ticket.

Checklist (tick each, or write the problem)
- Django's own check: run `manage.py check --deploy` with the production settings and read every warning.
- Login required everywhere except login, register, password reset pages (list them).
- Every POST form has a CSRF token; no view is exempt (search for csrf_exempt: should be zero results).
- Cross-site scripting: no `|safe`, no `mark_safe` on user text, no innerHTML with data (search the repo).
- SQL injection: no raw SQL or string-built queries with user input (search for `.raw(`, `.extra(`, `cursor.execute`).
- File access: the SnapGene file view cannot read outside its folder (try `../` by hand).
- Redirects: the login `next` parameter only allows our own addresses.
- Sessions: lifetime decided (for example 12 hours), cookies are HttpOnly, and Secure/SameSite are set for production.
- Passwords: Django's validators on, minimum length decided, the dev admin/admin account does NOT exist in production.
- Error pages: DEBUG off in production, a custom 403/404/500 page shows no technical details.
- Secrets: SECRET_KEY and the database password come from the environment, none is in Git history (run a secret scan over the history).
- Dependencies: pip audit (or GitHub Dependabot alerts) shows no known serious problems.
- Rate limiting of login attempts: see W6-L1.
Acceptance criteria
- ☐ Every line of the checklist has a result in the pull request; each failure has a ticket.

Contract for the frontend

Acceptance criteria
